task: Core #1186 F6-U03e: actual isolated PostgreSQL17 schema ACL restore and DDL event-trigger rollback rehearsal

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical F6 safety prerequisite. Require actual isolated PG17 role grant behavior, failure rollback and external dependency simulation with zero hosted database risk; distinguish hosted event function bodies (read-only) from fixture-only DDL triggers.

acceptanceCriteria: Real isolated PostgreSQL17 test proves DROP SCHEMA/CREATE SCHEMA does not preserve expected namespace privileges, whereas explicit allowlisted ACL restoration exactly restores fixture anon/authenticated/service/admin grants.
At least three injected error stages before/after drop and after regrant demonstrate transaction rollback preserves original ACL, row, external trigger and committed event audit.
Successful commit demonstrates recreated old application namespace, restored ACL, external trigger, and event audit visibility; negative missing-grant test fails closed.
Host/GitHub service identity, DB name, version, local network and inherited environment selectors are protected; only prefixed fixture schemas may be dropped.
Complete exact-head CI/Lifecycle, isolated PostgreSQL job and documentation mark scope LIMITED_TO_FIXTURE and hosted reset remains blocked.
invariants: Source ACL fragment never references a caller-chosen project or role and is never executed by a hosted runner.
Only dedicated disposable PostgreSQL17 GitHub service receives DDL with hardcoded f6_u03e_ prefix; no Supabase secrets or connection URL.
All necessary grants derive from F6-U03d read-only observed public/private namespace ACLs; forbidden extra grants fail.
Event-triggers simulator does not claim that six original Supabase-managed provider functions were executed.
No automatic or manual path in this unit can alter hosted platform, staging or Fresh Install projects.
forbiddenStates: Granting CREATE to anon or authenticated in the public namespace.
Granting private namespace CREATE to authenticated or service_role.
Committing recreation without ACL restoration or restoring the Auth-equivalent dependent trigger.
A failed transaction leaves altered namespace ACLs or a partial new schema.
Reporting a PostgreSQL fixture PASS as hosted migration proof or Alap/Pro RLS acceptance.

failureModes: Namespace dropped and recreated without original AUTHORIZED role grants but tests only check owner postgres.
Grant restoration silently grants too broad CREATE privilege to the anon or authenticated role.
SQL error leaves new schema committed but old Auth trigger removed, breaking registration.
Simulated event audit persists after transaction abort and falsely indicates a successful DDL replay.
Connection string/PGHOSTADDR directs fixture DDL to the hosted customer database.
Old source-only review unit is changed into actual hosted reset before provider triggers are proven.
edgeCases: PostgreSQL namespace owner privileges cannot be revoked and are not equivalent to explicit role grants.
Role ACL order/serialization differs while semantic USAGE/CREATE privileges remain equivalent.
DROP SCHEMA CASCADE removes an external trigger on auth-equivalent users and rollback restores it.
A fixture DDL event handler fires on CREATE SCHEMA and DROP SCHEMA and its audit rows roll back on error.
Delayed NOTIFY on transaction COMMIT differs from service readiness and is not treated as a PostgREST success proof.
Unexpected extra privilege to anon or authenticated is detected in explicit check functions.

alternatives.summary: Dedicated PostgreSQL17 CI fixture verifies schema grants and DDL callbacks with rollback/commit, no Supabase access.
alternatives.reason: Proves actual Postgres semantics needed before hosted authority, without touching provider-managed schemas.

alternatives.summary: Attempt direct hosted Fresh Install DROP/CREATE/GRANT and inspect resulting ACL.
alternatives.reason: Insufficient managed event-trigger and transactional guard proof; high data and provider risk.

alternatives.summary: Only lint GRANT statements without a real PostgreSQL role/DDL test.
alternatives.reason: Cannot prove actual grant semantics, cascade-dependent trigger or rollback.

specialistReviews.finding: A schema ACL restore with too-broad CREATE grants could let low-privilege clients alter DB objects.
specialistReviews.resolution: Whitelist separate USAGE and CREATE semantic role grants and assert forbidden grants absent in a real PostgreSQL service.

specialistReviews.finding: External triggers and event-audit effects must rollback with the DDL and be recreated in positive replay.
specialistReviews.resolution: Prove rollback from real fixture connections and a successful commit with original Auth-like dependency restored.

specialistReviews.finding: Local DDL callbacks are not equivalent to Supabase managed Auth/Storage/PostgREST provider functions.
specialistReviews.resolution: Record exact read-only function fingerprints and explicitly restrict proof to isolated PG17 semantics; later hosted proof separate.

specialistReviews.finding: PostgreSQL event-trigger callbacks and NOTIFY delivery are transactional, but a provider PostgREST schema reload is a separate external service action.
specialistReviews.resolution: Exercise local callback audit and rollback/commit; record the six genuine Supabase function fingerprints without treating them as production execution proof.

challenge.scenario: CREATE SCHEMA restores owner but drops guest/authenticated USAGE.
challenge.finding: Postgres namespace recreation loses named-role ACL entries.
challenge.resolution: Allowlisted explicit GRANT statements plus real role-based positive/negative checks in PG17 fixture.

challenge.scenario: Granting ALL PRIVILEGES to anon exposes schema CREATE despite RLS.
challenge.finding: Schema CREATE privilege is separate from table RLS.
challenge.resolution: Require only USAGE for fixture anon/authenticated roles; verify forbidden CREATE is absent.

challenge.scenario: SQL-drop event trigger not observed or incorrectly assumed to fire after rollback.
challenge.finding: DML audit and event notifications participate in transaction commit semantics.
challenge.resolution: Use disposable fixture event handlers with committed audit checks after rollback and positive commit; keep hosted provider effect unproven.

challenge.scenario: The external auth.users trigger is dropped on cascading function removal.
challenge.finding: Cross-schema dependent trigger must survive rollback and be recreated before any successful commit.
challenge.resolution: Dedicated auth-like schema fixture with callback and automatic presence checks.

challenge.scenario: A developer uses arbitrary psql URL/host in an otherwise fixture-only script.
challenge.finding: Could route DDL outside ephemeral Postgres.
challenge.resolution: Refuse PG* overrides, require GitHub ephemeral marker plus exact Docker service IP, database/user/version before executing fixture SQL.

challenge.scenario: Hosted PostgREST watcher source changes while the fixture still passes.
challenge.finding: Static simulation cannot prove provider functions.
challenge.resolution: Capture exact observed six event functions' digests; any future hosted transaction must revalidate and independently observe provider behavior.

challenge.scenario: The schema owner is postgres but a real low-privilege client inherits an unexpected role grant.
challenge.finding: Simple ACL string equality is insufficient; effective privilege checks must use explicit separate principal identities and deny CREATE for guest/authenticated.
challenge.resolution: Create separate fixture roles for each allowed role and use has_schema_privilege plus negative missing-grant and privilege-escalation assertions.

challenge.scenario: The transaction has a successful SQL DROP and schema recreation but a synchronous DDL event handler throws before COMMIT.
challenge.finding: Provider-like DDL hooks can abort transactions, and a local fixture should verify event handler failures preserve previous ACLs and Auth-like dependency.
challenge.resolution: Inject a fault from a disposable event-trigger callback in PostgreSQL17; demonstrate complete rollback of row, grant and external trigger.

Positive commit fixture with external trigger and observed event-audit changes after COMMIT only.
Record six hosted provider event-trigger fingerprints via read-only Supabase; describe limited scope and non-authorized reset.
Exact-head standard CI, TypeScript, Production Build, Completion Truth, Lifecycle closure. Hosted 59 migrations remain BLOCKED.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: F6-U03d discovered that the existing source-pinned, intentionally non-executable customer Fresh Install DROP/CREATE candidate omits exact public/private namespace ACL restoration. Six provider event triggers exist, including two PostgREST watchers. Prove namespace grant restoration and transactional DDL event behaviors in an isolated PostgreSQL 17 fixture without any Supabase write or production credentials.
observableOutcomes: An ephemeral PostgreSQL17 fixture demonstrates that DROP/CREATE removes namespace grants; an explicit known-only regrant restores exact usable privileges for fixture roles analogous to anon, authenticated, service_role, supabase_admin and owner.

Aborted fixture transactions restore old grants/data/auth-equivalent trigger and do not commit audit events; successful fixture replay recreates table and external trigger, restores ACLs, and commits only approved event-audit entries.

Captures read-only fingerprints of all six actual hosted Supabase event trigger functions; in particular the PostgREST DDL watchers issue NOTIFY pgrst reload schema on relevant DDL. Exact function-body hashes are observations, not equivalent proof of a simulated hosted service.
Existing F6-U03b abort-before-DROP still remains active; this unit ships only a locked isolated test process and a nonexecuting schema-regrant SQL fragment for later reviewed transaction assembly.
unresolvedRisks: Fixture event triggers cannot establish actual hosted Supabase event-trigger execution, PostgREST service readiness, or all provider-managed side effects.
Schema grants alone do not prove table/function/sequence ACLs or real actor tokens and RLS.
An unexpected additional pg_depend external reference, changed data, extension or live session must still abort hosted cleanup in its own future transaction.
Existing hosted Fresh Install app tables remain occupied; 59 reviewed customer baseline migrations have not run.

Exercise rollback fault injection before/after schema recreation and ACL repair plus a positive commit, proving original grants and external trigger remain correct after errors.
Record all six hosted event-trigger function hashes from read-only Supabase connector observation and distinguish actual provider functions from fixture examples.
Keep default and PR paths entirely non-destructive to Supabase: no hosted secret, no live SQL, no project toggles.
out: No modification of original hosted F6-U03b source compiler execution switch, schema, storage or Auth managed metadata.
No destructive live Supabase migration execution, direct API revoke/grant or role writes.
No Builder, Template Factory, second Control Plane or new cloud project.
No claim of full Fresh Install hosted 59-file, signed-in Office Alap/Pro or PostgREST integration readiness.
